correctness.rationale: The complete Bayer subset-facet system gives Euclidean supporting distances (H_k-k t)/sqrt(k); diagonal symmetrization and lower constraints yield r(k+sqrt(k))<=H_k-k. The center (1+r)1 attains all inequalities, and any active rank with lower-coordinate constraints proves uniqueness and precise tangencies. Strict convexity of t/(1+t) against 1/[t(1+t)] orders thresholds in the one-parameter b=(M+1,1,...,1,floor(M theta)) construction; strict phases persist for large integers. Redundant rank n-1 when b1=1 cannot minimize. Independent finite numerical inball examples corroborate, not prove, the theorem.
